audit.whatIsWrong: Six of seven chart rows said Renekton while the page's own whys say the opposite from level 3 onward: whys[2] 'flip the trade', whys[3] 'out-trading him', whys[4] 'kill him', whys[5] 'force every all-in', whys[6] 'out-duel him'. diffRating 8.5/10 and 'Hard matchup' sat next to diff EVEN and a 53.76% Jax win rate over 1557 games.
audit.why: Packet levelChart is Renekton / Skill / Jax / Jax / Jax / Jax / Jax and matches the prose. Renekton is an early bully with no scaling — his Dominus is 120s at rank 1 and gives health, while Jax's 110s ultimate gives resists and on-hit that only compound with items.
audit.corrected: Rows 1-6 flipped as matched pairs with ratings realigned; diffRating 5.5/10 and the difficulty and final-rating lines aligned to EVEN.

audit.whatIsWrong: Phase whys were generic and gave no numbers on a matchup that is entirely about one cooldown.
audit.why: Ruthless Predator is 16/14/12/10/8s — a 16-second window at rank 1 in which Renekton has no stun. Slice and Dice is 16s at rank 1 and is his only escape; Cull the Meek is a flat 7s heal that anti-heal answers.
audit.corrected: Phase whys rebuilt on Ruthless Predator's 16s and Slice and Dice's 16s.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two errors. (1) Jax's ultimate written as 'Grandmaster at Arms' in whys[4], whys[6], spikes[2].text, mid, late and wants.you[1] — six fields. (2) The page repeatedly instructs the player to 'hold Counter Strike through the empowered W stun to dodge it'. Ruthless Predator is a spell, not a basic attack, so it lands through Counter Strike's dodge.
audit.why: Counter Strike dodges basic attacks only, per Riot's own text. Telling a player his dodge negates a point-blank stun is the kind of instruction that gets him killed mid-combo. The correct use is to hold E for the autos and Cull the Meek that follow the stun, not to expect it to eat the stun itself. Worth also noting empowered Ruthless Predator destroys damage shields on the target.
audit.corrected: Grandmaster's Might in all six; the dodge reframed to 'his stun lands regardless — hold E for the autos after it'.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns names Ruthless Predator without a number, and Slice and Dice's cooldown is never given despite the page telling you to dive through it.
audit.why: Both are 16s at rank 1. Diving a Renekton whose E is down is a completely different proposition from diving one who is holding it.
audit.corrected: Numbers stated in the Level 3 and first-item phases.

edits.before: This is where you take over. His whole threat is the committed fury combo — empowered W stun plus cleaves — and Counter Strike eats exactly that: hold it through the burst, recast to stun him out of his own all-in, then grind. At 6 your Grandmaster at Arms is the wall: the Armor/MR burst shrugs off his empowered W damage while your third-hit magic proc and stacking attack speed shred him, and his only out is the second cast of Slice and Dice (E) — which you Leap Strike straight back onto. Force the all-in whenever his fury is spent and his empowered W is on cooldown — that's a dead Renekton.
edits.after: This is where you take over. His threat is the committed fury combo, and the key detail is that the empowered W stun is a spell — it lands through Counter Strike's dodge. Hold E for the autos and cleaves that follow it, then recast to stun him out of his own all-in. At 6 Grandmaster's Might is the wall: the Armor/MR burst shrugs off his empowered W damage while your third-hit magic proc and stacking attack speed shred him, and his only out is Slice and Dice (16s) — which you Leap Strike straight back onto. All-in whenever his fury is spent and his W is down.

edits.before: There is no late-game trap here — Renekton is not a scaler, he's an early bully who falls off a cliff once items come online, so the lane only tilts harder your way. Past two items your Grandmaster at Arms defenses and on-hit damage out-duel him in any straight 1v1, and he can't burst through your steroid the way he did at level 2 with full fury. Hunt him on the side lane, dive him through his Slice-and-Dice (E) escape, and don't let his early lead (if he got one) convince you to respect a fight you now win clean.
edits.after: There is no late-game trap here — Renekton is not a scaler, he's an early bully who falls off a cliff once items come online, so the lane only tilts harder your way. Hunt him on the side lane, dive him through his Slice-and-Dice (E, 16s) escape, and don't let an early lead of his convince you to respect a fight you now win clean.

notes: Two serious problems. Six of seven chart rows said Renekton while the whys[] said Jax from level 3 on — the chart claimed Jax loses a lane he wins at 53.76%. And the page told players four separate times to 'hold Counter Strike through the empowered W stun to dodge it'; Ruthless Predator is a spell and lands through the dodge, which dodges basic attacks only. Also 'Grandmaster at Arms' in six fields. Renekton's empowered W additionally destroys damage shields on the target — noted for anyone editing the itemization line later.
